entries.463f20e8f3e8ef4c: The company states that its strength lies in its four core technologies of metal, polymer, photonics and high frequency, and in its ability to contribute to solving social issues not only in each of these areas but also in converged areas not limited to specific markets. It cites as the source of its competitiveness that it has built relationships of trust with stakeholders across a wide range of fields and has refined its development and proposal capabilities over many years.

entries.56035b7ae5245cf3: Toward 2030, it plans to concentrate management resources in the data center domain, where demand continues to grow, and strengthen supply capacity and business foundations for optical-related products and heat-dissipation and cooling products for data centers. In addition, to meet demand for stronger transmission infrastructure arising from the expansion of renewable energy and high-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission, it states that it will newly establish a domestic production site for HVDC cables in Futtsu, Chiba Prefecture. For growth after 2030, it states that it will also work to create new businesses in areas such as life sciences, superconductivity and laser applications.
entries.61889f4fa1e1135f: It is a corporate group consisting of Furukawa Electric Co., Ltd. and its consolidated subsidiaries. It makes and sells products by applying technology developed in its three businesses of infrastructure, electrical and electronics, and functional products, and with 'Services and Development, etc.,' covering research and development and services, it forms four reportable segments. Consolidated headcount is 49,112 (as of March 31, 2026).

entries.709d097dbc921dd9: In infrastructure, it makes optical fiber and cables, optical semiconductor devices and power cables; in electrical and electronics, it makes automotive parts such as wire harnesses, copper wire, winding wire and wrought copper products; and in functional products, it makes heat-dissipation and cooling products, tape for semiconductor manufacturing and electrolytic copper foil.
entries.74844c90ba198dd6: From optical fiber and power cables to automotive parts and copper materials
entries.78d791390b8456e0: This business produces automotive parts and metal materials used in electrical and electronic equipment. It handles automotive parts (wire harnesses, steering, roll and connector products, battery condition detection sensors, peripheral monitoring radars, etc.), automotive and industrial batteries, copper wire and aluminum wire, winding wire and stainless steel wire, wrought copper products (strip, wire, bar), precious metal plated products, and specialty metal materials (shape memory and superelastic alloys, etc.), and manufacturing and sales are handled by the company, Furukawa ＡＳ Co., Ltd., Furukawa Magnet Wire Co., Ltd. and others. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥756,170 million, the largest of the four reportable segments and up from ¥727,690 million in the previous fiscal year. Employees numbered 34,934 as of March 31, 2026 (excluding temporary employees), and the majority of the Group's total of 49,112 employees belong to this business. In addition, the reportable segment classifications were reviewed at the beginning of the current period, and the previous period's figures have been restated under the revised classifications.
entries.7c0156be1a8a2605: No external customer accounts for 10% or more of consolidated revenue (fiscal year ended March 2026). Revenue by customer location was ¥645,598 million for Japan, ¥290,197 million for Asia (excluding China), ¥178,583 million for North and Central America, ¥125,685 million for China and ¥67,495 million for other regions, and the overseas revenue ratio was 50.6%. For data center–related business, it plans to expand contact with key customers, including major cloud operators, and make proposals from the stage at which product specifications are decided.
entries.7e1d298a2ac2a0e8: This is a field handling power cables and industrial electric wires and equipment. In the power business, amid steady demand for ultra-high-voltage underground lines in Japan and submarine and underground lines for renewable energy, it worked to expand production capacity and construction capability for power cables, and it transferred all equity interests in its Chinese subsidiary for the purpose of business restructuring. In the industrial wire and equipment business, after integrating the metal wire business within the group, it focused on expanding sales of priority products such as aluminum CV cable, which is lightweight, flexible and contributes to more efficient and labor-saving installation work, and plug-in connectors with cables, which can be used safely and quickly without special skills thanks to a mechanism preventing incorrect insertion.
entries.82adb24e797c128a: The company states that its strength lies in its four core technologies of metal, polymer, photonics and high frequency, and in its ability to contribute to solving social issues not only in each of these areas but also in converged areas not limited to specific markets.
entries.8321cf3ba1e506e5: Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥1,307,560 million, up 8.8% from ¥1,201,762 million in the previous fiscal year. External customer revenue was ¥756,170 million for Electrical and Electronics, ¥363,941 million for Infrastructure, ¥150,804 million for Functional Products, and ¥36,644 million for Services and Development, etc. As reasons for the increase, the company cites higher revenue from data center–related products such as optical fiber cables, higher revenue from automotive parts such as wire harnesses, and the impact of soaring copper ingot prices.

entries.9ba3ba73bd052235: Net income attributable to owners of the parent for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥72,514 million, up 117.4% from ¥33,357 million in the previous fiscal year. The company explains that, in addition to the boost from higher revenue, profit increased due to its efforts to improve productivity and optimize selling prices.
entries.9d0654f425d3d191: This segment supports the Group’s businesses through hydroelectric power generation, research and development of new products, real estate leasing, and contract services for various operations. It is carried out by Furukawa Nikko Hatsuden Co., Ltd. and others, and most of the electricity used at the Nikko Works is supplied by this hydroelectric power generation. The company positions this as contributing to the achievement of its sustainability target in the medium-term management plan of “a renewable energy share of 30% of electricity consumption.” Revenue from external customers in the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥36,644 million, the smallest of the four reportable segments, up from ¥29,754 million in the previous fiscal year. The number of employees was 2,356 (as of March 31, 2026, excluding temporary employees), and includes personnel engaged in company-wide operations such as headquarters departments. In addition, in a review of segment classifications at the beginning of the current fiscal year, some businesses previously included in infrastructure were transferred to this segment.

entries.b2a81dfa9d432e8a: This is a field producing copper materials used in electronic components and other products. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, as demand for electronics-related products showed signs of recovery, it expanded sales of high value-added products such as the oxygen-free copper product group and copper alloys for high-performance resistor materials. It is also working on optimizing selling prices and improving product mix, including withdrawing from low-profit product types. Although affected by soaring copper ingot prices and yen weakness, revenue in this field exceeded the previous period.

entries.bceb32717249770c: Net income attributable to owners of the parent for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥72,514 million, up 117.4% from ¥33,357 million in the previous fiscal year.
entries.be42f76aaea8ece5: Hydroelectric power generation, research and development of new products, real estate leasing, and contract services for various operations
entries.c2286e1343014b07: This is a business producing functional materials and components incorporated into equipment, such as resin, copper foil and heat dissipation components. It handles cable conduit materials, foamed products, tapes for semiconductor manufacturing, electronic components, heat dissipation and cooling products, aluminum blank material for hard disk drives, and electrolytic copper foil, and manufacturing and sales are handled by the company, Trocellen GmbH, Furukawa Copper Foil Co., Ltd., Taiwan-Japan Furukawa Copper Foil Co., Ltd. and others. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥150,804 million, up from ¥140,947 million in the previous fiscal year. Against the backdrop of brisk investment related to data centers and rising demand for renewable energy, it is focusing on expanding sales of high value-added products such as heat dissipation and cooling products, tapes for semiconductor manufacturing and electrolytic copper foil for high-frequency substrates, and a new plant for semiconductor manufacturing tapes began operating in fiscal 2025, enabling a stable supply of products. It is also affected by soaring copper ingot prices and the impact of exchange rates. Employees numbered 2,503 as of March 31, 2026 (excluding temporary employees).

entries.d10454c8871c24e6: In infrastructure, it makes optical fiber and cables, optical semiconductor devices and power cables; in electrical and electronics, it makes automotive parts such as wire harnesses, copper wire, winding wire and wrought copper products; and in functional products, it makes heat-dissipation and cooling products, tape for semiconductor manufacturing and electrolytic copper foil. In Services and Development, etc., it carries out hydroelectric power generation and research and development of new products, and hydroelectric power covers most of the electricity used at its Nikko Works.
entries.d5e818cf4fa1d2bc: This is a field building communications networks, centered on optical fiber and cable. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, against the backdrop of increased demand for data center-related products, it advanced the development and expansion of sales of high value-added products, including rollable ribbon cable used to build high-speed, large-capacity communication networks, MT ferrules as connector parts essential for optical communication, and DFB laser diode chips suited to faster communication speeds, and it also carried out capital investment to increase production capacity. It restructured the operating structure of its optical fiber and cable business so that decisions are made under a unified global strategy, and it set up a sales structure for optical fiber cable in North America.
entries.d723c26a23f84d3b: Customers for automotive parts, including those for the electric vehicle market
entries.dc86b281b3661c54: This is a field producing automotive parts such as wire harnesses. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, it worked to optimize selling prices in response to the impact of U.S. trade policy, exchange rates and rising labor costs, and it advanced the consolidation and optimization of production sites and the sharing and automation of production lines, supported by steady demand for wire harnesses in the domestic market. It is also working on developing and expanding sales of high-voltage-compatible wire harnesses for the electric vehicle market, and on expanding sales of aluminum wire harnesses suited to weight reduction. Because a subsidiary operating the battery business is no longer consolidated, revenue in this field was below the previous period.

entries.fb3ff72a23825d34: This business makes optical fiber, cables and other pathways for communications and electric power. It handles optical fiber, optical fiber cable, optical connection products, optical semiconductor devices, optical fiber fusion splicers, optical transceivers, network equipment, ＣＡＴＶ system, wireless products, power cables and connection parts, industrial electric wire, and power transmission and distribution components, and manufacturing and sales are handled by the company, Lightera, LLC, Lightera LatAm S.A., Lightera Japan Co., Ltd., Furukawa Electric Metal Cable Co., Ltd. and others. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥363,941 million, up significantly from ¥303,369 million in the previous fiscal year. Employees numbered 9,319 as of March 31, 2026 (excluding temporary employees). Following the review of reportable segment classifications at the beginning of the current period, some businesses previously included in this segment moved to Services and Development, etc., while some businesses whose costs were allocated to each segment as head office expenses moved into this segment. The figures for the previous period have been restated under the revised classifications.
